To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) type inference for languages with subtypes is NP-hard, (ii) if the subtype hierarchy is a lattice then type inference is in PSPACE, (iii) if the subtype ordering is variable, type inference is in NPSPACE.

type inference is NP-hard for monomorphic languages, PSPACE-complete for languages with a lattice subtype hierarchy, and polynomial-time solvable for languages without function constants and a fixed subtype hierarchy.
type inference is PSPACE-complete for a fixed subtype hierarchy, and is NP-hard for a fixed subtype ordering.
